_about: Documented exceptions to the Kubernetes hardening baseline checked by scripts/conformance/hardening.py. Keyed by workload name, then by check. An exception that no longer matches a finding is reported, so this list cannot quietly go stale. Workloads we write have almost none; the rest belong to the OpenShell chart, its driver and the SPIRE chart.

risk-guard.no_api_token_unless_needed: With the sandbox tunnel gate on, Risk Guard turns a tunnel's source address into a sandbox by reading supervisor pods. It does that as the service account risk-guard-tunnels, which can only get, list and watch pods. Without the gate the pod has no token.

openshell.no_api_token_unless_needed: The OpenShell gateway creates and deletes sandbox pods through the Kubernetes API.
openshell.secret_mounts_restricted: The OpenShell chart mounts its TLS and client-CA secrets with the default file mode. Not changed here because the chart owns the pod; tighten through chart values when it exposes them.
openshell.read_only_root: The OpenShell chart's gateway container writes to its root filesystem. Not changed here because the chart owns the pod.
openshell.requests: The OpenShell chart sets no resource requests for the gateway container by default.
openshell.memory_limit: The OpenShell chart sets no memory limit for the gateway container by default.

sandbox-workload-pod.requests: Created by OpenShell's Kubernetes driver from the sandbox's template; its memory and CPU come from the Kata runtime class and the VM, not container requests.
sandbox-workload-pod.memory_limit: Same as requests: the micro-VM is sized by the runtime class.
sandbox-workload-pod.read_only_root: The agent's root filesystem is writable by design (its workspace). Inside the micro-VM, Landlock and OpenShell's policy confine what it can write.

sandbox-supervisor-pod.requests: Created by OpenShell's Kubernetes driver; it sets no requests.
sandbox-supervisor-pod.memory_limit: Created by OpenShell's Kubernetes driver; it sets no limits.

spire-server.no_api_token_unless_needed: SPIRE's server and controller manager use the Kubernetes API (token review, pod and service account lookups, publishing the trust bundle).
spire-server.no_privilege_escalation: SPIRE chart installed with its recommendations switched off (global.spire.recommendations.enabled=false). Turning them on needs the CA subject set, which changes the CA; deferred until SPIRE can be re-issued on purpose.

spire-agent.no_api_token_unless_needed: The SPIRE agent attests workloads by asking the kubelet and the API server who a process is.
spire-agent.no_host_access: The agent shares the host PID namespace and publishes its socket through a hostPath, because that is how it identifies a workload's process.
spire-agent.non_root: The agent runs as root to read other processes' attributes.
spire-agent.no_privilege_escalation: As for non_root. Also: chart recommendations are off (see spire-server).

spire-spiffe-csi-driver.no_api_token_unless_needed: The CSI driver's registrar talks to the kubelet and the API server.
spire-spiffe-csi-driver.no_host_access: A CSI node driver has to mount into pods through hostPath directories under the kubelet.
spire-spiffe-csi-driver.non_root: The CSI driver performs mounts, which needs root.
spire-spiffe-csi-driver.no_privileged: The CSI driver mounts into other pods' filesystems, which needs privileged mode (mount propagation). This is the one genuinely privileged component.

spire-spiffe-oidc-discovery-provider.no_api_token_unless_needed: The provider reads the SPIRE agent's workload API through a CSI volume and the API server for its configuration.
